decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY capturing support for both motors, solenoids, and fans under load without exceeding power-system limits.
Power-supply load capacity does not change the solenoid valve's actuation, isolation, or closed-state behavior.
The electrical capacity requirement does not alter the whisk head's size, material, style, or positioning criteria.
Power-supply capacity does not change the selected bowl capacity, form, or size priorities.
Requiring adequate electrical capacity does not necessarily change the off-the-shelf component strategy or custom spout strategy.
The power-system load requirement leaves the expected smooth and frothy mixing result unchanged.
Electrical load capacity has no necessary effect on bowl, whisk, or spout cleaning behavior.
The power-capacity decision does not modify the leak, seepage, sealing, or closed-valve drip constraints.
Adequate power-system capacity does not itself change the established splash-control target or methods.
The basic wiring-plan deliverable remains required, and the source does not establish a specific wiring-plan change.
Power-supply load capacity does not alter bowl removal, clearance, or swapping behavior.
The capacity requirement does not modify the existing 3000 RPM maximum, adjustment range, or normal-operation constraint.
